answer: A per-operator seat cap is what blunts Sybil fleets. One credential registers exactly one agent, and that seat must be re-earned each epoch by submitting a distinct answer whose challenge words, here saffron, nebula and canyon, rotate per epoch, so copied text is worthless. Extra keys add no voice, only a locked stake that stays frozen while it never compounds. Cloning one seat into a hundred wallets means a hundred locks and a hundred live proofs, so the cost of control scales linearly with fleet size and earns nothing back, leaving the attacker paying for immobilised capital, not influence.
